text_blocks.snippet: Losartan is a prescription medication—commonly known by the brand name Cozaar—used to treat high blood pressure, protect kidneys in people with type 2 diabetes, and lower the risk of stroke.
While most people tolerate it well, it can cause several side effects.

list.snippet: Dizziness or lightheadedness (especially when standing up quickly)
Upper respiratory infections (cold-like symptoms, stuffy or runny nose, sore throat)
Digestive issues (mild nausea, diarrhea, or heartburn)

text_blocks.snippet: (Note: Mild symptoms like dizziness or headaches often improve after a few weeks as your body adjusts to the medication.)
Contact your doctor immediately or get emergency help if you experience:

list.snippet: Signs of a severe allergic reaction: Swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat, or trouble breathing or swallowing (anaphylaxis)
High potassium levels (hyperkalemia): Muscle weakness, confusion, or a fast or irregular heartbeat
Kidney problems: Little to no urination, swelling in your hands, ankles, or feet, or unexplained weight gain
Very low blood pressure: Severe dizziness, feeling faint, or passing out
Liver problems: Yellowing of your skin or eyes (jaundice) or severe upper stomach pain
Pregnancy Warning: Losartan can cause serious harm or death to an unborn baby. You must stop taking it immediately if you become pregnant.
Do Not Stop Suddenly: Never stop taking losartan without consulting your healthcare provider, even if you feel well, as stopping abruptly can cause your blood pressure to spike.

text_blocks.snippet: You can read more detailed prescribing and safety information via the Mayo Clinic Losartan Guide or GoodRx Losartan Side Effects Overview.
